learn.title: Identity, access and security
objectives: Describe Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Entra Domain Services, and when to use each.
Explain authentication methods: SSO, MFA and passwordless.
Describe external identities (B2B collaboration and customer identities with Microsoft Entra External ID).
Explain Conditional Access and Azure role-based access control (RBAC).
Describe Zero Trust and the defense-in-depth layers.
Describe the purpose of Microsoft Defender for Cloud.
concepts: Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft's cloud identity and access management service (formerly Azure AD). It holds users, groups and app registrations, and provides sign-in, SSO, MFA and Conditional Access for Azure, Microsoft 365 and thousands of SaaS apps.
Tenant
A dedicated instance of Microsoft Entra ID that represents one organisation.
Microsoft Entra Domain Services
Managed domain services (domain join, Group Policy, LDAP, Kerberos and NTLM) for legacy apps, without deploying or patching domain controllers. Microsoft runs the domain controllers.
Authentication vs authorisation
Authentication proves who you are. Authorisation decides what you're allowed to do. Authentication happens first.
Single sign-on (SSO)
Sign in once, then use many applications without signing in again.
Multifactor authentication (MFA)
Requires two or more factor types: something you know (password), something you have (phone, key) and something you are (fingerprint, face).
Passwordless
Signing in without a password, using Windows Hello for Business, Microsoft Authenticator or FIDO2 security keys.
External identities
Let people outside your organisation sign in with their own identities: B2B collaboration (guest users) and customer identity for consumer-facing apps (Microsoft Entra External ID).
Conditional Access
Entra ID policies that use signals (user, location, device, app, risk) to decide whether to allow access, block it, or require something extra such as MFA.
Azure RBAC
Grants access to Azure resources by assigning a role to a security principal at a scope (management group, subscription, resource group or resource). Assignments are inherited by child scopes.
Zero Trust
Never trust, always verify. Its principles are verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, and assume breach.
Defense in depth
Layered security: physical, identity and access, perimeter, network, compute, application and data.
Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Security posture management (secure score, recommendations) and workload threat protection for Azure, hybrid and multicloud (AWS and GCP) resources.
comparisons: Entra ID: cloud, web protocols (OAuth, OpenID Connect, SAML), flat structure. AD DS: on-premises, Kerberos and LDAP, organisational units (OUs) and Group Policy.
Entra ID vs Entra Domain Services
Entra ID is modern cloud identity. Entra Domain Services adds managed traditional domain features for legacy apps.
Conditional Access decides whether and how you can sign in. RBAC decides what you can do with Azure resources after you sign in.
RBAC controls who can perform actions. Policy controls which resource configurations are allowed, whoever deploys them.
Owner: full access, including assigning roles. Contributor: manage everything but can't grant access. Reader: view only.
B2B: partners and suppliers work in your tenant as guests. Customer identities: the public signs up for your consumer app.
traps: A password plus a security question is still one factor type (something you know), so it isn't MFA.
Entra Domain Services doesn't give you Domain Admin rights or access to the domain controllers.
Entra directory roles (such as Global Administrator) and Azure RBAC roles are separate systems.
RBAC permissions are additive: the effective access is the union of all role assignments.
Defense in depth starts with physical security on the outside and ends with data at the centre.
Conditional Access needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher. Security defaults are the free alternative for baseline MFA.
revision: Entra ID = cloud identity. Entra Domain Services = managed legacy domain features.
MFA = two or more of: know, have, are.
Passwordless = Windows Hello for Business, Authenticator, FIDO2.
RBAC = who + what role + which scope, inherited downwards.
Zero Trust = verify explicitly, least privilege, assume breach.
Defense in depth layers: physical → identity → perimeter → network → compute → application → data.
Defender for Cloud = secure score, recommendations, threat protection across Azure, on-premises, AWS and GCP.
